- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Roberto Clemente grew up in Puerto Rico, signed with the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1954, played for their minor league team, and was known for his charitable work and activism, especially in support of Puerto Rico and Latin America. He died in a plane crash delivering aid in 1972.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Curtis Granderson grew up in Chicago, was drafted by the Detroit Tigers in 2002, and has a Grand Kids Foundation supporting positive youth development in underserved communities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] CC Sabathia grew up in Vallejo, California, was drafted by the Cleveland Indians in 1998, and started the PitCCh In Foundation with his wife to support youth in underserved communities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ken Griffey Jr. grew up in Cincinnati, Ohio, was drafted by the Seattle Mariners in 1987, and has supported the Boys and Girls Clubs of America for over 20 years.

- [USER] User inquired about other players who have done similar philanthropic work.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Jackie Robinson broke the color barrier in MLB in 1947, grew up in poverty in Pasadena, California, and founded the Jackie Robinson Foundation for minority youth scholarships.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Curtis Pride was born deaf, grew up in Washington, D.C., played in the major leagues, and founded the Together With Pride Foundation for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Joe Panik grew up in Hopewell Junction, New York, played for the San Francisco Giants, and established the Joe Panik Scholarship for students at his high school.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Andrew McCutchen grew up in Fort Meade, Florida, played for several major league teams, and started the Cutch's Crew Foundation to support youth in underserved communities.
